confusables: See you tomorrow (A2-0893 — check its staging for a watch); What time is it? (A2-0379, asked of a stranger)

confusables: No, thank you (A2-1987, the covered cup); I don't have time (A2-0915)

lithuanian: Ar nori arbatos? / Ar norite arbatos?

distinguishing_cue: the offered cup in both hands, eyebrows up
confusables: No, thank you (A2-1987); Here you are (A2-0885, a parcel across a counter)

confusables: Do you like…? (A2-1992, the host's raised eyebrows while the guest tastes); I liked it! (A2-1183)

new_staging: a kitchen table; a tray with a cup of coffee and a glass of tea; a woman draws the glass of tea toward herself with her RIGHT hand and pushes the coffee an inch away with her LEFT, looking at her host with a smile; the host looks at her. distinguishing_cue: one drawn in, one pushed away
confusables: I don't mind (A2-1946, shrug at two cups); I would like coffee (A2-0917)

lithuanian: Ar tau patinka…? / Ar jums patinka…?
new_staging: a kitchen; a guest tastes soup from a spoon, eyes to the ceiling, thinking; the cook stands with the ladle, eyebrows raised, head tilted, looking at the guest's face. Insets: the spoon; the pot on the stove
distinguishing_cue: the cook's raised eyebrows watching the taster
confusables: I don't like… (A2-1990); Bon appétit (A2-0889)

confusables: Yes, you may (A2-1994, the next moment); Is this seat free? (A2-2023, a train seat with a bag on it)

distinguishing_cue: the nod and the palm turned to the chair
confusables: May I? (A2-1993); Please / Prašau (A2-0357, now a held door for a pram); Sit down, please (A2-1166)

english: How do you spell it? / Spell it, please

confusables: Write it down, please (A2-0903, two panels); What is your name? (A2-0366)

english: Do you understand? / Is that clear?

distinguishing_cue: the teacher's pause and raised eyebrows, the pupil's frown
confusables: I don't understand (A2-0371); I understand (A2-0372)

confusables: Who's calling? (A2-1998, hand over the mouthpiece); hello on the phone (A2-1171, lone woman lifting the receiver)

new_staging: a hallway; a woman holds the receiver with her RIGHT hand and covers the mouthpiece with her LEFT palm, head turned to a man in the sitting-room doorway, eyebrows up; he looks at her and shrugs. Insets: the covered mouthpiece close; the man in the doorway
distinguishing_cue: the palm over the mouthpiece and the head turned away from the phone
confusables: Could I speak to…? (A2-1997); Hold on a moment (A2-1999)

new_staging: a hotel reception; the receptionist holds the receiver lowered to her collarbone with her LEFT hand and raises the index finger of her RIGHT hand to a guest who has just come up to the desk, looking at him; he waits, hat in hand. Insets: the raised finger close; the desk bell
distinguishing_cue: the receiver lowered and one finger up to a second person
confusables: Just a moment (A2-0884, no telephone — check its staging); Who's calling? (A2-1998)

new_staging: a kitchen; a man in an apron holds the receiver a hand's width from his ear and looks at it with a puzzled frown, his other hand open and empty; nobody else in the room. Insets: the telephone on the wall; a shrug of one shoulder
distinguishing_cue: the receiver held away and looked at
confusables: hello on the phone (A2-1171, receiver to the ear, mouth opening); Pardon? (A2-2020)

new_staging: a park bench; a young man holds a small notepad and pencil ready, pencil tip on the page, looking at the young woman beside him; she looks at him and counts something off on her fingers; the pad is turned so its page is edge-on and blank; a telephone kiosk behind them. distinguishing_cue: pencil poised on a blank pad, the kiosk behind
confusables: What is your address? (A2-2002, house number plate); How old are you? (A2-1157, fingers counted — here a pad and a kiosk)

distinguishing_cue: the finger at the house-number plate
confusables: Where is…? (A2-0378); Where do you live? (A2-1159 — check its staging)

new_staging: LEFT: a woman indoors by a frosted window hugging herself, shoulders up, breath faintly visible, a cold stove behind. RIGHT: a man on a sunlit bench fanning his face with his cap, collar open, a glass of water beside him; two different people, two places, each panel complete
distinguishing_cue: the hug and the fanning cap, side by side
confusables: It is cold today (A2-0923, the weather, not the body); hot/cold adjective cards

new_staging: a building site at the end of the day; a worker sits slumped on a plank bench, legs out, cap pushed back, eyes half shut, both arms hanging, spade leaning beside him; a mate standing by looks at him and offers a flask. Insets: the spade in the earth; boots unlaced
distinguishing_cue: the slump, the hanging arms
confusables: to go to bed (A2-1180); Everything is fine (A2-1161)

lithuanian: Dešinėje. / Sukite į dešinę. / Sukite į kairę.

new_staging: a village road; a visitor with a suitcase asks a man on a bicycle; the cyclist holds up his RIGHT hand with finger and thumb a centimetre apart and nods toward the church tower a field away, looking at the visitor; the visitor looks at the gap between his fingers. distinguishing_cue: the finger-and-thumb gap, the tower within sight
confusables: How do I get to…? (A2-0957, map); Go straight ahead (A2-0959)

confusables: I would like coffee (A2-0917); One ticket to Kaunas (A2-2026, one finger at a ticket window — different window, a train behind)

new_staging: a market stall; the stallholder, a woman in an apron, has filled a customer's string bag and holds it half-offered in her LEFT hand, her RIGHT hand open palm-up over the piled vegetables, eyebrows raised, looking at the customer; the customer looks at the goods. confusables: That's all, thanks (A2-2009, the next moment); Do you have…? (A2-1168)

distinguishing_cue: the purse snapped shut and the nod
confusables: Anything else? (A2-2008); Thank you (A2-0358)

new_staging: a taxi at a kerb; through the open passenger door the driver, half-turned in his seat, holds out a few coins on his open RIGHT palm; the passenger, already standing on the pavement with his bag, waves them off with his RIGHT hand, palm toward the driver, and smiles at him; the driver looks at him. distinguishing_cue: coins offered and waved off
confusables: How much does it cost? (A2-0377); Stop here, please (A2-2029, inside the taxi, pointing at the kerb)

new_staging: a street kiosk; a visitor holds up a small flat battery between finger and thumb toward the kiosk seller, eyebrows up; the seller leans out and points with his RIGHT arm along the street, looking at her; she looks at the battery. Insets: the battery close; the kiosk window with blank magazines
distinguishing_cue: a small object held up and an arm pointing away down the street
confusables: Where can I find…? (A2-0909, two panels); Is there…? (A2-0382); Do you have…? (A2-1168)

new_staging: MERGE CANDIDATE with A2-0964 Ar galite ką nors rekomenduoti? Insets: the finger on the menu line; a dish on a tray
distinguishing_cue: the menu turned to the waiter and his finger on a line
confusables: Can you recommend something? (A2-0964); I'll have the soup (A2-2038, the diner taps the menu, the waiter writes)

new_staging: a meeting room; a man hurries in through the door, coat half off one shoulder, his RIGHT hand raised flat in apology, looking at the seated people; six people at a long table turn their heads to him; the wall clock shows a quarter past. Insets: the clock face; the door still swinging
distinguishing_cue: the hurried entrance, the raised flat hand, the clock
confusables: I'm sorry (A2-0881, the boy with the football); Excuse me (A2-0362, the trolleybus bump)

new_staging: a hospital corridor; an anxious young woman sits on a bench twisting a handkerchief; a nurse sits beside her, her RIGHT hand laid over the young woman's hands, looking at her face with a calm smile; the young woman looks at the nurse. Insets: the hands together close; a closed ward door with a round window
distinguishing_cue: the hand laid over the fretting hands, the calm face
confusables: it's nothing; never mind (A2-1185); worried / susirūpinęs (A2-1883, mother at the window)

new_staging: outside a theatre; a woman in a good coat stands before a poster frame on which a diagonal blank strip has been pasted across a picture of a dancer; she presses her RIGHT hand to her cheek, mouth open in a small 'oh'; her companion beside her looks at her and spreads his hands. Insets: the pasted strip across the poster close; two tickets in a gloved hand
distinguishing_cue: the hand to the cheek before the cancelled poster
confusables: a pity / gaila (A2-1150, now the dropped ice cream and the brother); No way! (A2-1184)

new_staging: a pavement; a child sits holding a grazed knee, a fallen bicycle beside her; a man kneels in front of her on one knee, both hands open toward her, head tilted, looking at her face; she looks at him with wet eyes. Insets: the bicycle on its side; a handkerchief being offered
distinguishing_cue: the kneeling man with open hands at the fallen child
confusables: I need help (A2-0906); Help! (A2-1181)

new_staging: a family table in spring light; a grandmother hands a painted egg across the table to a small boy; a dish of painted eggs, a willow sprig with catkins in a jar, a plaited loaf; both look at each other. Insets: two children knocking eggs together; the willow catkins close
distinguishing_cue: the painted eggs and the catkin willow
confusables: Happy holidays / Su šventėmis (A2-1165, snow, sprig of fir, a counter); Merry Christmas (A2-1164)

new_staging: two neighbours parting at a garden gate; the one inside the gate has just spoken and the one outside answers with his RIGHT hand raised open at shoulder height and a broad smile, looking back at him; the first looks at him and raises his own hand; a basket of apples on the gatepost. Insets: the two raised hands close; the apples
distinguishing_cue: two mirrored raised hands and smiles at a gate
confusables: Goodbye (A2-0354, one man waving back at a woman on a step) — here both hands up, both men at the gate, no bag; Have a good weekend (A2-1162)

new_staging: an office at lunchtime; a man leaves through the door with his jacket slung over his RIGHT shoulder and lifts two fingers of his LEFT hand in a casual salute to a colleague at a desk, looking at her; she looks up from her typewriter and nods; a wall clock shows twelve. Insets: the two-finger salute close; his empty chair with the jacket gone
distinguishing_cue: the casual two-finger salute, jacket over the shoulder, midday
confusables: Bye (A2-0356); See you (A2-0355); See you tomorrow (A2-0893) — check their gestures and give each a different hand sign

new_staging: a market; an old man leans toward a stallholder with his head turned so his RIGHT ear is toward her, his RIGHT hand cupped behind that ear, eyebrows up; the stallholder, a step back behind her boxes, looks at him with her mouth open mid-word. Insets: the cupped ear close; the stall's scales
distinguishing_cue: the head turned ear-first, not the face
confusables: Could you repeat? (A2-0374, a woman at a telephone kiosk, hand behind the ear) — the same gesture; if QA reads it as 0374, MERGE and keep 0374

new_staging: a farm yard; two farmers shake hands (both RIGHT hands) across a cart of potato sacks, each with his other hand on the cart rail, both nodding and looking at each other; a set of scales and a folded banknote on the sack between them. Insets: the handshake over the sacks close; the scales
distinguishing_cue: a handshake over goods and money: a bargain struck
confusables: Nice to meet you (A2-0363, a handshake with an introducer in a meeting room) — here no third person, a cart and scales; Of course (A2-0883)

new_staging: a conference room; a man has risen from his chair at a long table, RIGHT hand flat on his chest, LEFT hand on the chair back, looking at the people across the table; they look at him; a blank name card on the table before him. Insets: the hand on the chest close; the blank name card
distinguishing_cue: standing up at a table with the hand on his own chest
confusables: My name is… (A2-0367, A2-0910 — check their stagings; if either has a hand on the chest, give this card the standing-up and the name card); This is… (A2-1983, palm toward another person)

english: Excuse me, is this seat free?

Insets: the bag on the seat; the luggage rack
distinguishing_cue: a train seat with a bag on it, pointed at
confusables: May I? (A2-1993, a café chair, hand on its back); window seat / aisle seat (A2-1189/1190)

distinguishing_cue: the purse opened over the goods at a shop counter
confusables: The bill, please (A2-0381, a restaurant); Can I pay by card? (A2-0954)

new_staging: a hotel desk; a traveller with a suitcase at her feet rests her RIGHT hand on the desk and looks at the receptionist; the receptionist runs his finger down an open ledger of plain ruled lines and looks up at her with a nod; a row of keys on hooks behind him. Insets: the finger on the ledger line; a key with a numbered-looking blank tag
distinguishing_cue: the ledger being checked, the keys behind
confusables: I would like to book a room (A2-0951); Do you have…? (A2-1168)

new_staging: a station ticket window; a passenger holds up ONE finger of his RIGHT hand to the clerk behind the glass and looks at her; she looks at him, hand on the ticket roll; through the hall doors a green train. Insets: the ticket coming out of the slot; the clerk's hand on the roll
distinguishing_cue: one finger at a ticket window with a train behind
confusables: How much does the ticket cost? (A2-0928, two panels, money); One coffee (A2-2007, if kept); Which platform? (A2-2027)

new_staging: a station hall; a passenger holding a ticket looks between two numbered-looking blank platform signs hanging over two arches, and asks a porter, who points with his RIGHT arm through the left arch, looking at her; a departures board as a blank panel. Insets: the two platform arches; the ticket in her hand
distinguishing_cue: two platform arches and the porter's arm choosing one
confusables: Where do I have to change? (A2-0955, now aboard with a map); Where is…? (A2-0378)

lithuanian: Ar šis autobusas važiuoja į centrą?

Insets: the blank route board over the windscreen; the open door with its step
distinguishing_cue: one foot on the step, the question to the driver, the arm pointing ahead
confusables: Where do I have to change? (A2-0955); Stop here, please (A2-2029)

new_staging: inside a taxi; the passenger in the back seat leans forward between the front seats and points with her RIGHT hand past the driver's shoulder at the kerb outside the windscreen; the driver glances at her in the mirror; a chequered band on the dashboard. Insets: the kerb through the windscreen; the meter as a blank box
distinguishing_cue: leaning forward in the back seat, the finger at the kerb
confusables: Keep the change (A2-2010, outside the taxi); Go straight ahead (A2-0959)

new_staging: a street; a pale man holds his RIGHT side with his RIGHT hand and leans on a lamp post, asking a passer-by; the passer-by, a woman with a shopping bag, points with her RIGHT arm toward a shopfront with a green cross sign a few doors away, looking at him; he looks where she points. Insets: the green cross sign close; a doctor's bag
distinguishing_cue: the hand pressed to the side and the green cross pointed to
confusables: Call a doctor! (A2-0907, two panels, urgent); I don't feel well (A2-0961); It hurts here (A2-0962)

english: I have a temperature / a cold

Insets: the thermometer close; a bowl of lemons and honey
distinguishing_cue: the thermometer shown, the red nose, the handkerchief
confusables: Get well soon (A2-0892, visitor with flowers); I don't feel well (A2-0961)

new_staging: a pharmacy counter; the pharmacist in a white coat holds up TWO fingers of her RIGHT hand beside a small pill box she holds in her LEFT, looking at the customer; on the box a small sun and a small crescent moon are drawn as symbols; the customer nods, looking at the fingers. distinguishing_cue: two fingers and the sun-and-moon box
confusables: I'm allergic to… (A2-0963); I need a doctor / pharmacy (A2-2030)

new_staging: a school yard; children with rucksacks climb into a coach; a mother at the door waves both hands high and laughs, looking at her son at a window; the boy at the window waves back with a grin; a rolled tent on the roof rack. Insets: the tent on the roof rack; a fishing rod poking from a rucksack
distinguishing_cue: children off on an outing, a coach with camping kit, both hands up in glee
confusables: Have a good journey (A2-0895, now the conductor and the suitcase at a train); Have a good weekend (A2-1162)

new_staging: a clothes shop; a customer between two rails of coats raises her RIGHT palm gently toward an approaching assistant, with a polite smile, her LEFT hand still on a hanger, looking at him; the assistant stops and inclines his head. Insets: the raised palm close; a hanger on the rail
distinguishing_cue: the gentle raised palm to the approaching assistant
confusables: Can I help you? (A2-1984, the assistant's open hand — the question this answers); No, thank you (A2-1987, the covered cup)

distinguishing_cue: the dress held against herself, the curtain
confusables: Do you have it in another colour? (A2-2037); It's too big (A2-2036)

Insets: a boy in a jacket whose sleeves stop at the forearm; the sleeve over the hand close
distinguishing_cue: the sleeves over the hands, and in the inset the sleeves too short
confusables: Can I try it on? (A2-2035); big / small adjective cards

english: Do you have it in another colour / size?
lithuanian: Ar turite kitos spalvos? / kito dydžio?
new_staging: a clothes shop counter; a customer holds up a blue jumper by the shoulders toward the assistant and looks at her; the assistant, looking at the customer, reaches with her RIGHT hand to a shelf behind her where the same jumper lies folded in red and in green.
